source.title: Scaling Large Language Models for Next-Generation Single-Cell Analysis
source.authors: S. Rizvi; Daniel Levine; Aakash Patel; Shiyang Zhang; Eric Wang; Curtis Perry; Ivan Vrkic; Nicole Mayerli Constante; Zirui Fu; Sizhuang He; David Zhang; Cerise Tang; Zhuoyang Lyu; Rayyan Y. Darji; Chang Li; Emily Sun; David Jeong; Lawrence Zhao; Jennifer Kwan; David Braun; B. Hafler; Hattie Chung; R. M. Dhodapkar; P. Jaeger; B. Perozzi; J. Ishizuka; Shekoofeh Azizi; D. van Dijk

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present. Scaling-curve figures are referenced but their plotted values are not included in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether scaling with model capacity improves held-out downstream task performance, using task metrics rather than held-out language-model loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results for downstream single-cell tasks, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It does not test small-run prediction of much larger runs, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or architectural-shape invariance. The curves in Figure 4 are not numerically available in the supplied text; the paper describes their trends in prose. The increase in training samples for a fixed 27B model is recorded separately because it is data scaling, not a direct test of the listed size-or-loss wording of V6.
record.test_reason: The study trains C2S-Scale models from 410M to 27B parameters on single-cell 'cell sentence' data, plus a data sweep at 27B. It reports downstream task performance against scale, a new setting for V6. It fits no power law and reports no held-out pretraining loss, so only V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that scaling C2S-Scale up to 27B parameters, and training data at fixed size, systematically improves single-cell task performance under both full and LoRA fine-tuning, mirroring NLP scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Uses model-capacity sweeps and downstream single-cell task metrics rather than held-out next-token cross-entropy scaling fits; does not test compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports scaling trends both for full fine-tuning and LoRA; it also reports performance gains from more training samples at fixed 27B capacity.
record.problems: The scaling figures' numerical values are not available in the supplied text; scaling evidence is described qualitatively. The paper reports downstream task metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss, and provides no fitted scaling exponents or small-to-large extrapolation test.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible scaling outcomes were separately reported in the supplied text. Other task evaluations do not compare model size or training-data scale.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute is reported.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No loss curves or power-law fit in the single-cell or fine-tuning setting. Only qualitative downstream improvement is reported, so whether the same power-law form holds is untested.
No quantitative fit or prediction of larger-model performance from smaller ones, and no link to pretraining loss. Only monotone improvement is described.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The authors call this 'scaling laws', but no functional form, exponent or loss is reported. The reader's V5 labels and the V6 limits_scope labels are dropped because the missing quantification marks untested parts, not results that qualify the version. The size axis spans two model families (Pythia 410M/1B, Gemma 2 2B/9B/27B), which confounds parameter count with base model and pretraining. No uncertainty is reported for the scaling figures.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study reports qualitative downstream performance scaling for single-cell transcriptomic tasks, but does not fit or report a power-law form, exponents, or scaling over several orders of magnitude.
Performance is measured on held-out downstream tasks; the paper does not test a quantitative predictor based on pretraining loss.
Dependence of exponents or compute-optimal allocation on parameter counting, schedules, data, or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: C2S-Scale fine-tuned models, 410M–27B, single-cell downstream tasks (full fine-tuning and LoRA), and data scaling at 27B

relationships.display_finding: Performance improved consistently with capacity and with training samples at 27B, although the size sweep combined Pythia and Gemma 2 models.
